stem:
Esha marks three distinct points P, Q, and R on her paper that do not lie on one straight path.

How many distinct lines are determined by these points?

options.text: One line, because any set of points always lies on a single line.
Infinitely many lines, because one point alone already fixes infinitely many lines.
Three lines: PQ, QR, and RP, because each pair of distinct points determines exactly one line.
Nine lines, by multiplying three points by three possible directions.

teacher.key_rationale: Any two distinct points determine exactly one line. The three pairs PQ, QR, and RP give three lines. One point alone does not fix a unique line, and the points are not collinear.
